video_title: “It’s NOT CLOSE” Golden Tate on Stafford vs. Russell Wilson + Winning a Super Bowl

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate compares the quarterback skills of Russell Wilson and Matthew Stafford
quotes.excerpt: pure quarterbacking skills is not even close
quotes.quote: Everyone would always ask me, so who do you think is a better quarterback, Russell Wilson or Matthew Stafford? Both really good quarterbacks, but pure quarterbacking skills is not even close.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate explains why he joined the Special Forces reality show
quotes.excerpt: I felt like I needed a new challenge in life

text_blocks.speaker: Brice Butler
text_blocks.text: What made you get on the Special Forces show?

text_blocks.speaker: Golden Tate
text_blocks.text: When you watch the show, it looks hard, but it don't look that hard. I felt like I needed a new challenge in life, so I was like, all right, I'm going to go check it out.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate reflects on the lessons learned from the Special Forces show
quotes.excerpt: I learned some things in life that I need to focus on and be better at
quotes.quote: After doing it and lasting up until the last day, I'm glad I did it because I learned some things in life that I need to focus on and be better at. Yes, it was the hardest thing I've ever done, but as you know, when it comes to military, it's about discipline.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate discusses his leadership style as a football player
quotes.excerpt: I've never been much of a who-rah type of leader
quotes.quote: As a football player, I've never been much of a who-rah type of leader. I've been like, all right, I'm going to go out here and practice, I'm going to make some plays, I'm going to go out here in the game, I'm going to make some plays. I'm going to just make it happen. And that's a great leadership skill to have.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on transitioning from football leadership to family leadership
quotes.excerpt: I'm no longer performing on the football field, I am performing within my family
quotes.quote: I'm no longer performing on the football field, I am performing within my family. And so I need to be able to vocalize to my wife and lead her and my children versus just going out here and doing something. I need to teach them like that.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on dealing with failure during his time on Special Forces
quotes.excerpt: I struggle with it. I'd rather not do something than fail
quotes.quote: I struggle with it. I'd rather not do something than fail. And I have a good grasp on like what I can achieve and what I can't achieve, I feel like. And so it was tough for me because I felt like I was embarrassing. I felt like I was letting people down when I failed a mission.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on the mental challenge of losing control in Special Forces
quotes.excerpt: we lose all sense of control
quotes.quote: What made this harder in my opinion was that we lose all sense of control. You lose all your sense of like time, you lose all your freedom, you lose like you don't know when, you don't know when things are happening.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on the value of military-style training for criminals
quotes.excerpt: I think people, the most evil and messed up criminals in the world, I think it's the easy way out
quotes.quote: I think people, the most evil and messed up criminals in the world, I think it's the easy way out for them is to go to jail. I think you go put them in one of these camps for a year or two years or however long, a month, whatever it is, and I think that is going to be plenty of punishment because it is it's it's brutal.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on his time with the Seattle Seahawks
quotes.excerpt: the beginning of my career was like almost like a little fantasy dog
quotes.quote: The beginning of my career was like almost like a little fantasy dog. My time in Seattle was awesome. And I didn't learn that until after I left. I was like, man, we had it good, dog. I got drafted in the second round, 60th overall pick. In my opinion, I thought I should have went in the first round, but mentally I was not ready to be a first rounder.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on Pete Carroll's influence and his departure from Seattle
quotes.excerpt: he left me to go with you
quotes.quote: I am so grateful that Pete Carroll was coaching straight from SC. He left me to go with you. I'm still upset about that, Pete.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on the impact of Matthew Stafford and Calvin Johnson
quotes.excerpt: we got a gunslinger in Matt Stafford. We got Calvin Johnson
quotes.quote: We got a different type of quarterback, we got a gunslinger in Matt Stafford. We got Calvin Johnson, and I believe this is when YAC King, Golden Tate emerged. Obviously, when you were in Seattle, you were learning how to play the position. You get to Detroit and now like you're a guy.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on the play-extending ability of Russell Wilson
quotes.excerpt: he was a play extender
quotes.quote: Russell Wilson, when I had him, I mean, he was a play extender. And so a lot of times, it was like having two plays every single time a play was called, because it was the play that you ran the routes, but you always had to figure that he's going to get outside the pocket and extend his play.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on Russell Wilson's deep ball accuracy
quotes.excerpt: his deep ball was so nice and it was so high and would just hit your fingers like soft
quotes.quote: What separated Russell to me was his deep ball. His deep ball was so nice and it was so high and would just hit your fingers like soft. I just, when Russell Wilson threw me a go ball, I just had options. I had options to slow down a little bit, run up under it and catch it.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on Matthew Stafford's arm talent and precision
quotes.excerpt: his arm talent, his arm, you know, his arm strength, how precise he was and how smart he was
quotes.quote: Matthew Stafford had a huge part in me being YAC King. His arm talent, his arm, you know, his arm strength, how precise he was and how smart he was, played the biggest part in me being like the YAC King.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on Matthew Stafford's immediate success in Los Angeles
quotes.excerpt: he went to LA with Sean McVay, a mastermind
quotes.quote: He went to LA with Sean McVay, a mastermind call plays. I was absolutely not surprised that he had a immediate success. He went to LA with Sean McVay, a mastermind, call plays.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on the chaotic nature of being traded in the NFL
quotes.excerpt: being traded is chaotic
quotes.quote: Being traded is chaotic. It is chaotic. And to give you something that a lot of the world might understand is, can you imagine working your job that you've worked in my case four and a half, five years, you have your family, you have your home, you have all your stuff, and we'll just say, we'll just say you work at Enterprise. You work at Enterprise and you show up to on your off day, they call you and say, hey, Emily, you thank you for your work. You've been great. You've been one of our top salesperson people in the company, but we are going to transfer you to Philadelphia effective immediately. Thank you so much. Goodbye.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on his recruitment to Notre Dame
quotes.excerpt: I got recruited by Notre Dame
quotes.quote: I got recruited by Notre Dame, I'm going to Pope John Paul II High School, which is a Catholic school, and people are just saying, dude, you got to go check out Notre Dame. I knew I wasn't going to UT because my parents weren't letting me go to UT, but I wanted to go to Florida State. I wanted to go to Florida. I wanted to go anywhere, LSU. I wanted to go in the SEC, but I took a trip, I just took a trip and I went to South Bend, Indiana in December or January.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on his decision to play football and baseball at Notre Dame
quotes.excerpt: I saw opportunity to come in as a freshman and make an impact
quotes.quote: They let me go there and play football and baseball. I saw opportunity to come in as a freshman and make an impact. I knew if I went to Notre Dame, I was going to be pro ready because Charlie Weis was just now coming from the league and he has like two, three, four rings at this point. And if I graduated, I was going to be okay in life.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on his legacy beyond football statistics
quotes.excerpt: my legacy has nothing to do with a single down or a single football play
quotes.quote: As a pure, as legacy only related to football and NFL ball, I hope I'm always remembered as like a grinder, like a YAC King. And I hope I inspired like younger generation that you don't have to be the 6'2, you don't have to be the blaze of speed, but you got to have that dog in you. And just the just the fight, just to fight, scratch and claw, and you can do this. And so like hopefully I'm just known as just a dog, like how I think of Heinz Ward, how I think of Steve Smith, like those type of guys. But when I even use that word legacy, man, my legacy has nothing to do with a single down or a single football play I've ever made. I hope my legacy is that one, I brought people to Jesus, I stewarded that God's gifts correctly, I led my family with integrity.

quotes.speaker: Golden Tate
quotes.summary_phrase: Golden Tate on his personal legacy and faith
quotes.excerpt: I love my wife and I just love Jesus. And so like that's what I want my legacy to be.
quotes.quote: I love my wife and I just love Jesus. And so like that's what I want my legacy to be. I want people to meet me and hang out with me and be like, man, I had a good conversation. And we had a couple of those conversations. And I think that's what life's about, man. Because the doors of heaven, man, this chain, these shoes, my golf swing—I hope my golf swing go with me, but it probably won't—but ain't none of this stuff going to be at the doors of heaven, man. But your heart and your soul will live forever, whether it's with Jesus or with the enemy.
